title: Hom for finite-dimensional algebra modules commutes with extension of fields
statement: Let $K$ and $L$ be fields [def-weil-field] and let $\iota:K\to L$ be a unital field homomorphism. Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional unital associative $K$-algebra, meaning a unital associative ring with a homomorphism $K\to Z(A)$. Let $V,W$ be finite-dimensional $K$-vector spaces with unital left $A$-module structures compatible with their $K$-actions. Write $\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,W)$ for the $K$-vector space of additive maps $f$ satisfying $f(av)=af(v)$. Form $A_L=L\otimes_K A$, with $(x\otimes a)(y\otimes b)=xy\otimes ab$, and $V_L=L\otimes_K V$, $W_L=L\otimes_K W$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(x\otimes a)(y\otimes v)=xy\otimes av$. Then the canonical $L$-linear map $$L\otimes_K\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,W)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{A_L}(V_L,W_L),\qquad x\otimes f\longmapsto\bigl(y\otimes v\mapsto xy\otimes f(v)\bigr)$$ is bijective. For $W=V$ it preserves multiplication by composition and the identity, hence is an $L$-algebra isomorphism on endomorphism algebras.

source.place: Tag 087R, lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext (1), is the commutative-ring analogue only. proof.text: Every $A$-linear additive map $f$ is $K$-linear: $f(cv)=f((c1_A)v)=(c1_A)f(v)=cf(v)$. For $x\in L$ set $T_{x,f}(y\otimes v)=xy\otimes f(v)$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] makes this a well-defined $L$-linear map. It is $A_L$-linear, since on generators both $T_{x,f}((z\otimes a)(y\otimes v))$ and $(z\otimes a)T_{x,f}(y\otimes v)$ equal $xyz\otimes af(v)$. The assignment $(x,f)\mapsto T_{x,f}$ is additive in both variables and $K$-balanced, as $\iota(c)xy\otimes f(v)=xy\otimes cf(v)$. It therefore induces the displayed map $\Phi$, which is $L$-linear by the same formula.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product (tensor universal property); agent coefficient-matrix argument, construction of the canonical intertwiner map

proof.text: The unital map $\iota$ is injective: for $c\ne0$, $\iota(c)\iota(c^{-1})=1$. Identify $K$ with its image in $L$. Choose finite spanning lists for $V,W$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and discard any vector in the span of its predecessors; the surviving lists are finite bases $(v_j)_{j=1}^n,(w_i)_{i=1}^m$. By [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], after flipping the tensor factors, $(1\otimes v_j)$ and $(1\otimes w_i)$ are $L$-bases of $V_L,W_L$. Thus a linear map is determined by its $m\times n$ coefficient array in these bases. Choose a $K$-basis $(b_s)_{s\in I}$ of the vector space $L$ using [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector]. Given any $F\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A_L}(V_L,W_L)$, each of its finitely many entries has a finite expansion in this basis. Taking the union of these supports gives a finite $S\subseteq I$ and arrays $F_s\in K^{m\times n}$ with $[F]=\sum_{s\in S}b_sF_s$. Define $f_s:V\to W$ by $f_s(v_j)=\sum_i(F_s)_{ij}w_i$ and extend $K$-linearly.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product (tensor universal property); agent coefficient-matrix argument, finite matrix coordinates and independent scalar coefficients

proof.text: For each $a\in A$, let $P_a,Q_a$ be the coefficient arrays of its actions on $V,W$. They have entries in $K$, since those actions are $K$-linear by the assumed compatibility. $A_L$-linearity of $F$ implies $[F]P_a=Q_a[F]$, by applying $F$ to $(1\otimes a)(1\otimes v_j)$. Substitution gives $\sum_{s\in S}b_s(F_sP_a-Q_aF_s)=0$. Entry by entry the coefficients in parentheses lie in $K$; independence of the $b_s$ forces $F_sP_a=Q_aF_s$ for every $s,a$. Evaluating this identity on each $v_j$ and then taking $K$-linear combinations gives $f_s(av)=af_s(v)$ for every $a,v$. Hence $f_s\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,W)$. The tensor $\sum_{s\in S}b_s\otimes f_s$ maps under $\Phi$ to a map with array $[F]$, so it maps to $F$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product (tensor universal property); agent coefficient-matrix argument, coefficient extraction from every intertwining equation

proof.text: Let $t$ lie in the kernel of $\Phi$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $t=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\otimes g_i$ with $g_i\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,W)$. From the finite list $(g_i)$ discard a vector whenever it lies in the span of its predecessors. The surviving maps $h_1,\ldots,h_k$ are $K$-linearly independent and span all $g_i$, so tensor bilinearity rewrites $t=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j\otimes h_j$. Their coefficient arrays $H_j\in K^{m\times n}$ are $K$-linearly independent: a zero linear combination of arrays is a map zero on all the $v_i$, hence the zero map. Flatten these arrays into vectors in $K^{mn}$. Apply [lem-weil-linear-independence-field-extension] with the given $K\to L$: the arrays remain $L$-linearly independent. Since $\Phi(t)=0$, its array $\sum_j\lambda_jH_j$ vanishes, and thus every $\lambda_j=0$. Therefore $t=0$ and $\Phi$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product (tensor universal property); agent coefficient-matrix argument, injectivity via independence of the coefficient arrays after field extension

proof.text: For $W=V$, equip $L\otimes_K\operatorname{End}_A(V)$ with $(x\otimes f)(z\otimes g)=xz\otimes(f\circ g)$. On $y\otimes v$, both $\Phi(x\otimes f)\circ\Phi(z\otimes g)$ and $\Phi(xz\otimes(f\circ g))$ take the value $xzy\otimes f(g(v))$. Pure tensors generate all the tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so additivity gives multiplicativity for arbitrary elements. Also $\Phi(1\otimes\operatorname{id}_V)(y\otimes v)=y\otimes v$, giving the identity. Together with $L$-linearity and the proved bijectivity, this is the claimed $L$-algebra isomorphism.
